A persistent conjecture posits that global symmetries cannot exist within quantum gravity. By examining extensive families of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories, the possible generalized global symmetries and mechanisms to avoid them are investigated. Essential components in these theories are generalized $\theta$-terms, which establish non-linear couplings among axion fields and terms topological quadratic in gauge curvatures, thereby disrupting many global symmetries. Any resulting residual symmetries can also be broken if certain charged states exist. We demonstrate, however, that generalized $\theta$-terms induce a generalized Witten effect; the implication is that a lattice of infinitely charged states forms. Furthermore, it is established that this lattice originates from the monodromy transformation of both the imaginary and real parts of the axiom. Consequently, these findings support the generalized conjecture that charged global symmetries cannot exist in quantum gravity.

Users typically run essential security applications alongside potentially harmful software on smartphones, relying heavily on faith in the device's hardware and system architecture to properly isolate (sandbox) these malicious programs—a trust that is frequently unwarranted. Our objective is to drastically reduce both the quantity and intricacy of components required for this sandboxing process by integrating a hardware architecture featuring multiple computation domains, each with its own trust level. In return, software executing security-critical tasks gains access to robust protections, while other programs operate with fewer constraints. We implemented this design on an FPGA and developed optimized versions of OpenSSL 1.0.2 and AES-ECB routines for execution within them, resulting in virtually identical OpenSSL performance to standard ARM+LITTLE systems and roughly 17% slower AES performance.

This study addresses robust reinforcement learning in environments subject to adversaries who corrupt both rewards and transitions at every step of an episode. Our proposed attack model involves an adaptive adversary capable of arbitrary manipulation within at most an \(\epsilon\)-proportion of total learning episodes, representing a capability strictly superior to that considered in previous researches. Our initial findings demonstrate that no existing strategy can secure a policy better than \(O(\epsilon)\)-optimal given this specific attack scenario. Conversely, we discovered that the natural policy gradient (NPG) technique unexpectedly preserves intrinsic robustness regarding bounded reward corruption and succeeds in locating an \(O(\sqrt{\epsilon})\)- optimal policy. Multi-phonon states linked to the local mode to-cavity (LMM) in semiconductor quantum dots have attracted significant research attention recently. Diverse engineering and scientific fields face continuous-time dynamic optimization challenges, ranging from real-decision implementation to simulation, often lacking analytical solvability. Whether prioritizing real-decision speed or computational ease, these solutions typically rely on two strategies: discretizing time and system models, or employing model predictive control (MPC). This work proposes utilizing neural network approximations within an MPC framework to solve such continuous-time optimization problems while retaining continuous variables, thereby circumventing discretization limitations. Specifically, this approach formulates problem objectives and constraints as neural network functions mapping states to costs and trajectories around paths of high density and variability. By reconfiguring standard gradient-based optimization algorithms to operate under an MPC scheme centered on neural networks, the system achieves real-decision-time computational feasibility. Unlike traditional methods, this technique preserves the integrity of continuous variables, enabling exact, discretization-free solutions.

Delineating esophageal tumors in CT scans presents a dual challenge for manual and automatic segmentation: the low radio-opacity of the surrounding airways and the close anatomical proximity to the vertebral column. While existing methods predominantly rely on fully supervised approaches, acquiring large volumes of annotated data necessary for these methods remains costly and cumbersome. Consequently, this study introduces a novel semi-supervised framework using deep convolutional neural networks to enhance automatic segmentation of esophageal tumors from limited labeled datasets. The model employs an encoder-decoder U-Net architecture enhanced with residual connections and dense block modules, utilizing total variation regularization within a supervised loss function tailored for the specific application. A key innovation is an entropy estimation module integrated into the training loss, designed to drive the accurate prediction of healthy regions surrounding the tumor. The study further establishes a fully automated segmentation pipeline specific to this task, utilizing the model for inference on labeled image patches and extending the trained weights to estimate outcomes on unlabeled samples. Performance validation was conducted against nine expert-annotated whole-tumor and two specific sub-tumor region labels (gross tumor volume and tumor margin) across 50 cases. Results demonstrate a significant improvement over a baseline semi-supervised system trained on only five annotated tumors, achieving superior accuracy with the proposed method trained on the same data (mean IOU of 0.7855 and 0.8558, and mean volume error of 18.60% and 9.16

Offshore drilling incurs significant expenses, particularly when hydrocarbons exist in complex reservoirs; consequently, optimizing well placement is vital for maximizing production. However, determining the optimal well trajectory requires precise knowledge of well logs and subsurface earth models, both of which typically contain uncertainties. To maximize production from wellbores equipped with multiple laterals, real-time adjustments along each trajectory become essential. Providing real-time recommendations for drilling parameters and inferring reservoir properties from well logs constitutes a key application known as geosteering. This process relies heavily on accurate earth models, despite the inherent data limitations. To optimize geosteering, this paper introduces a statistical methodology for smoothing and interpolating well logs via a stochastic approach grounded in Cartesian coordinates. This model incorporates local regularization based on a multi-scale filter applied directly in spherical coordinates to mitigate directional effects on log data. Since model parameters are subject to uncertainty in this framework, this study employs an ensemble method to estimate the ensemble of parameters. Using synthetic reservoir data, the proposed technique successfully smoothes well log datasets while effectively capturing spatial continuity that standard kriging often overlooks. Ultimately, these enhancements offer improved reservoir characterization for geosteering applications.

Named entity recognition (NER) stands as a pivotal task in natural language processing and core technique for knowledge extraction, extensively utilized to derive information from texts for subsequent applications. Nested NER, a sub-variant of NER, aims at identifying named entities where one entity is completely embedded within another. However, numerous prior studies model these inherently hierarchical nested entities using an inadequate linear structure. To rectify this structural discrepancy, the current approach models all nested named entities within a sentence as an integral holistic structure, introducing a corresponding parsing algorithm. Additionally, addressing the current absence of corpus-level context in such research, we incorporate corpus-level information through a specific method. Experimental results demonstrate that this model outperforms several established baselines on the OpenSubtitles dataset, offering enhanced entity extraction capabilities.

This study extends tropical methodologies to address arithmetic enumeration issues, specifically within the Grothendieck-Witt framework and regarding rationality over Henselian valued fields. Using these extensions to analyze plane quartic curves, we determine that there are $24\mathbb{i}$-equivalence classes of tropical bitangents. By establishing an enumeration framework grounded in valued fields, we identify the valuation types encompassed among the twenty four and apply known results on finite field bitangents to compute the $\mathbb{i}$-enumerated count of quartic bitangents in rational settings.

Defined as advanced capability in two or more languages for both spoken and written communication, multilingualism frequently manifests through code-switching or code-mixing within individual sentences. This work reviews existing natural language processing (NLP) literature regarding its limitations and obstacles when addressing five critical social impact areas: crisis response, healthcare support, political engagement, anti-disinformation strategies, and hate speech mitigation in multilingual communities. Furthermore, we introduce prospective datasets, models, and utilities poised to propel multilingual NLP research toward broader societal benefits. Utilizing English-Hindi mixing as a case study allows for representative inferences applicable to other languages pairs.

Automatic image description models are typically built and assessed on crowd-sourced human-generated references, with the crowdsource component serving as a baseline for future automatic image description tasks. This paper describes a systematic approach for establishing such baseline descriptions, which involves aggregating diverse sample image links for each entry in the dataset to form robust baseline alternatives. Applied specifically to the Flickr8k corpus, this method yielded a baseline of 50 alternative image links per caption, ready for use. Subsequent analyses by two additional studies using identical metadata but implementing different baseline images resulted in descriptions containing significantly fewer diverse links; they gathered just 2.1 and 2.15 images per caption respectively, with significant variance due to the limited number of diversification links in their systems. In contrast to these limited baselines, we propose a simple yet computationally efficient algorithm that provides optimal alternative image linking based on maximizing caption similarity, ensuring high diversity. Using metrics to quantify description quality—specifically "number of diverse links" and "similarity score"—our baseline achieved significantly higher diversity compared to the methods tested in those studies.

Tantalum oxides (Ta$_2$O$_5$) exhibit favorable physical and chemical traits, including strong antireflective capabilities and high dielectric constants. In addition, recent studies suggest that Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanoparticles could enhance biological efficacy in cancer hadron therapy, and first-principles simulations offer a robust method for exploring their electronic structures. While prior research has examined the effect of hydrogen adsorption on the tantalum dimer surface, the electronic properties of nanoparticles embedded within a host medium remain less understood. This study employs a computational model of Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanoparticles surrounded by a water environment to investigate their ground-state characteristics using the linearized augmented plane wave method within the density functional theory framework. Results indicate a marked discrepancy between these findings and those derived from gas-phase calculations, demonstrating both the essential role of water confinement in accurately describing nanoparticle properties and how environmental interactions significantly influence the material's physical behavior.

Previous studies have established that individual traits like personality and cognitive abilities significantly influence the sharing of misinformation. In this study, we investigate whether these individual-level mechanisms contribute to the geographic variability in news dissemination by analyzing data from Facebook news tracking between March 2017 and December 2018. Our dataset comprises over 200 million news exposure events and more than 32 million user profiles from the Lightcast data source, enriched with American Community Survey information on Big Five traits, fluid intelligence, news consumption habits. Using negative binomial regression, we examined how conscientiousness, emotional stability, and cognitive ability affect misinformation sharing volume, controlling for age, education, political affinity, news frequency, and network characteristics. Key findings indicate that both higher emotional stability and conscientiousness correlate with increased sharing of misinformation. Specifically, a one standard deviation rise in conscientiousness was found to be associated with a 14% surge in misinformation shares among participants whose news exposure did not exceed the median; among users with above-median exposure, the effect was even more pronounced, with misinformation shares rising 55% for the same increase in conscientiousness. These results suggest that the impact of such individual traits is likely amplified regarding misinformation propagation among individuals with larger, more diverse social networks.

We introduce HALFADO: a lightweight, semi-supervised algorithm designed to identify suspicious events within high-volume data streams. Contemporary supervised anomaly detection methods demand significant computational resources to maintain model accuracy, a limitation that also forces the use of expensive network connections for continuous updates. HALFADO offers a viable alternative by leveraging low-cost, private access to historical data for initial offline training, requiring only a minimal amount of labeled data from the actual target stream to bootstrap operations. Once initialized, the algorithm functions entirely within a standalone environment, completely eliminating the necessity for persistent internet connectivity as streams continue to arrive at an device locally.

Building upon the concept of "self-training," HALFANA relies intrinsic characteristics of the specific data at hand to detect and neutralize malicious or noisy points, thereby maintaining robustness against sudden concept shifts driven by adversaries or technical faults. In contrast to competing semi-supervised methods, the algorithm remains computationally efficient with constant memory usage, proving both faster in execution and more accurate than leading-state-of-the-art algorithms when processing stream data with sparse labeling. Practical experiments across various sparse-labeling scenarios confirm that the implementation of HALFANA has been deployed in an live monitoring system for a financial transaction database, effectively detecting fraudulent and suspicious financial activities.

Finally, to assess the practical significance of these findings, another experiment demonstrates that attention mechanisms focused on an instructor’s audio-visual cues enable a collaborating robot to anticipate the timing and execution of actions more accurately.

Few-shot learning is dedicated to categorizing new classes using minimal labeled examples. Despite notable advancements in this field recently, the majority of current methods rely on computing averages for data clustering prototypes and remain hindered by outliers. Addressing this issue, we present a straightforward yet potent framework tailored to few-shot classification. By integrating an episodic prototype generation component, the system successfully creates robust representative profiles from sparse support sets that remain highly accurate even for distant classes. Empirical results indicate that this module not only matches the accuracy of S-state-of-the-art models but also demonstrates greater consistency and accuracy in meta-learning tasks within a continuous setting.

Cross-domain recommendation (CDR) has gained significant traction in recent years due to its potential to enhance user experiences. Nevertheless, existing approaches frequently introduce negative transfer issues, arising when learned information harms performance. In this paper, a more effective CDR framework is introduced. The proposed model leverages multiple sparse domain configurations, enabling the co-learning of both comprehensive and domain-specific implicit domain features. These domain settings are dynamically adjusted based on the sparsity levels of user-item interaction matrices to ensure robust learning. Key components, such as Cross-Domain Collaborative Cross-Domain Correlation (CDCCR) and Multi-Sparse Domain Configuration (DSDF), are developed to facilitate shared learning across domains and sparsity levels. Furthermore, the model is designed to generate accurate, domain-tailored recommendations. Ultimate evaluation results, confirmed by experiments, demonstrate that the approach significantly enhances recommendation precision compared to other leading CDR methodologies.

Numerous convex optimization problems are limited by exotic cones, which remain relatively unexplored. This paper investigates two specific cases: the negative definite cone for general matrices and a subset known as the negative definite cone for commutative matrices. We establish connections between these cones and classical operators, including the Lorentz cone, the squared Euclidean distance function, and others. Additionally, we address the task of projecting onto these sets; we confirm that efficient projection algorithms exist for the commutative subset and offer practical guidance on constructing projections for general cases by leveraging connections to already-projected classical operator cones. Lastly, the abstract mentions exploring how these projections inform optimization, specifically examining the duality gap when projecting common convex optimization problems' convex sets.

Rapid advancements in image analysis have fueled a surge in automated quality control (QC) systems for MRI data. However, attaining broad applicability and robustness remains challenging. To address this, we introduce a standardized framework for evaluating MRI QC algorithms, complete with an open repository of metrics. We recognize that algorithmic performance is influenced not just by the method itself but also by the specific indices used to designate low-quality scans; consequently, our framework necessitates the assessment of multiple quality indices to ensure reliability and transparency. Using a vast collection of 10,000 healthy structural MRIs spanning 12,000 participants, we assessed four widely adopted QC algorithms across six distinct image index thresholds to identify index-related biases in the algorithms. Findings indicate that index parameters significantly sway both the quantity of misclassified images and the specific types of misclassification—such as elevated false-negative or false-positive rates—thereby underscoring the critical need for index-related QC measures within automated systems. To achieve robust and generalizable performance, we recommend implementing at least two index-independent QC algorithms within practical applications and offer guidance for future QC development. All components of this framework, including the metric suite and image dataset, are publicly accessible via an open repository at https://mriqc-evaluation.github.io/.

This paper examines the impact of privately owned electric vehicles on power system stability during disruptions. To capture the decentralized interactions within transportation and energy domains, we introduce a Network-based Multi-Agent Optimization with Equilibrium Constraints (N-MOPEC) framework. Specifically designed for a high-dimensional non-convex problem, our solution employs a specialized algorithm relying on precise convex reformulation. Extensive numerical experiments validate both the proposed methodology's efficacy in visualization and its potential policy ramifications, establishing a robust basis to advance resilience research on integrated transportation-power networks influenced by private EVs.

The release of the Intel Optane DC Persistent Memory Module (Optane DC PMM) has finally made scalable nonvolatile DIMMs a commercial reality. This emerging nonvolatile DIMM architecture supports byte-granularity access with memory-latency speeds, while ensuring data persistence against power outages. Nevertheless, the usage of Optane DC PMMs presents several challenges. First, current management tools and libraries often lack full support for its full byte-addressable capabilities. Second, developers must make difficult choices regarding allocation granularities and whether to configure the module in dense mapping or interleaved paging modes relative to system RAM. This study presents an evaluation of the module's performance across various workloads operating in both mapping and interleaved configurations. In addition, we perform single-threaded and multi-threaded benchmarks, analyze the impact of different libraries and runtime environments, and discuss the impact of software optimizations on overall performance. Our analysis reveals that despite the widespread adoption of Optane DC PMMs since 2017, significant performance gains are frequently attainable by utilizing specific software configurations and development practices. For instance, in certain scenarios, interleaved paging outperforms dense mapping while reducing cache set associativity; similarly, in workloads like those tested in MongoDB and certain MySQL configurations, custom data structures yield better results than standard OS-level allocators. Overall, our research indicates that Optane DC PMMs significantly enhance the execution time of diverse applications when deployed with optimized software architectures.

We examine predictions from the bilepton model, an extension of the standard model grounded in the gauge group $SU(4)_\text{L}$ and containing only three generations of fermions. Modifications to the standard model within this bilepton model are explored through tree level. We analyze the gauge bosons, their mass eigenstates, the implications of the resulting bilepton masses, and the interactions of these bileptons with other particles. Our analysis focuses specifically on the decay modes of diagonal tri-lepton bileptons and the associated physical eigenstate mixing of gauge bosons. Additionally, we investigate potential two-body decay modes of the off-diagonal mesonic states into various bilepton forms and the production processes of these mesonic states via W boson decay. Predictions concerning future physical experiments are also provided.

The Orbit Generating Systems (OGS) for non-abelian groups offer a meaningful extension of the canonical basis found in finite abelian groups. An OGS is characterized by the unique representation of each group element as a specific, ordered product of powers of designated generators. While R. Immune incompatibility between a recipient and donor represents a critical obstacle to kidney transplantation, often necessitating prolonged dialysis due to rejected organs. Utilizing first-principles calculations combined with dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the electronic structure of the flat band feature observed in oxygen-stoichiometric cuprate superconductors (specifically cuprates with optimal doping). This mechanism clarifies why similar flat bands do not appear in iron-based superconductors, as the $s_z$ orbital, which would need to form such a band, experiences negligible correlation-driven changes in its Fermi velocity. Consequently, the result provides explicit evidence countering theories proposing that the flat band in optimally doped cuprates forms from $s_{xy}$ or $d_{z^2}$ orbitals.

Storage is vital for providing firm power in decarbonized electric systems. However, retrospective analyses often reveal that storage providers may neglect acting on robust pricing signals during periods of scarcity. Although this phenomenon has traditionally been blamed on pricing failures or modeling defects, this paper argues instead that it stems from the widespread adoption of greedy dispatch algorithms combined with a risk-averse behavior inherent in dynamic programming approaches. Vehicular Communication (VC) protocols significantly contribute to accident avoidance by facilitating warning transmissions, yet manual driving at intersections often limits safety because drivers may react too slowly after detecting conflicts. Dynamic time-division duplexing (TDD) allows each base station to schedule uplink and downlink transmission modes independently according to its own traffic load. This paper investigates the deployment of differential privacy (DP) within graph-structured environments. It examines various DP formulations applicable both to publishing data and associated statistics, and to conducting machine learning on graph-based information, specifically focusing on graph neural networks (GNNs). A primary difficulty in adapting DP for this domain arises because data points are highly interconnected through complex, nonlinear, and sparse relationships, which complicates the assessment of individual privacy loss, particularly in differentially private learning contexts. Furthermore, the field lacks a unified or standard definition of DP for graphs, creating additional hurdles that negatively impact private learning using GNNs and render this endeavor challenging overall. Recognizing these gaps, we introduce a comprehensive framework that systematically compares different DP formulations for graphs and explores corresponding private learning strategies tailored for GNNs. We identify that the direct $\epsilon$-DP definition is most suitable for ensuring privacy within graph-structured data releases, whereas the proximal $\epsilon$-DP formulation, or the release of a learned model trained on graph data, are optimal choices respectively. The experimental section validates our proposed methods through a series of tests.

Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) technology has recently gained significant traction due to its ease of deployment, low cost, and minimal space requirements. The following work focuses on the thermomechanical modeling of crystallization driven by deformation in polymers that lack reinforcing agents. Given that this phenomenon markedly alters a material's mechanical and thermal behavior, it must be integrated into both manufacturing planning and the intended application of final products. To simultaneously address both thermal and mechanical aspects, we adopt a thermodynamic framework grounded in Coleman-Gohde split theory. Within this framework, the material is defined by two decomposed polymer chains populations—a crystalline fraction and an amorphous fraction—connected through reversible processes of nucleation and propagation. Since unfilled polymers often experience substantial volumetric thermal expansion, our model explicitly addresses shrinkage constraints arising from the crystalline expansion being restricted by an established, elastic host matrix. Consequently, internal thermal gradients can emerge within the material. The theoretical framework is complemented by a coupled system of partial differential equations, which is resolved numerically using a robust, efficient implicit scheme. This approach ensures the model's practical relevance by accounting for the interplay between competing factors: deformation-induced and temperature-induced driving forces for crystallization, as well as kinetic limitations.

This study examines a doped Bi$_2$Se$_3$ topological insulator exhibiting spin-triplet nematic superconductivity under an in-plane magnetic field, utilizing the mean-field theory of superconducting gaps. The investigation focuses on doped holes in the valence band structure composed of p-orbitals and analyzes superconducting states with various symmetries, including s$\pm$, sxsy, and ns$\pm$ nematic options. We calculate thermodynamic and transport properties for these superconducting phases, with particular emphasis on normal-state resistivity, Hall coefficient, and the anomalous resistivity anomaly associated with the superconducting nematic transition. A key finding is that even weak spin-orbit coupling can flip the system's chirality, transforming it from type A (antiparallel magnetization and chirality) to type B; under this condition, both nematic superconductivity and the resistivity anomaly persist or even strengthen. Additionally, employing the ANL model parameters for doped chiral topological superconductivity in Bi$_2$Se$_3$ allows us to account for experimental data regarding resistivity, the anomalous resistivity anomaly, and the Hall coefficient while nematic superconductivity develops.

Conventional non-coherent differential detection for continuous phase modulation (CPM) demonstrates significant robustness against channel impairments like phase and Doppler shifts. Discovered in 1995 as the initial T-dwarf, GJ 229B has been extensively observed spectroscopically; however, no contemporary spectroscopic analysis of its atmosphere currently exists. Existing data reveals distinctive spectral anomalies and conflicting recent dynamical estimates of its mass and orbit that require resolution. Situated tens of AU from its star, GJ 229B resides on the planetary or sub-planetary boundary, making it an ideal candidate for testing methods like Full Spectroscopic Retrieval (FSR)—a technique currently applied only to objects closer to stars. By analyzing four decades of Spitzer Space Telescope data via the FSR method, we successfully calculated its atmospheric spectrum. The analysis yields a 2 sigma posterior mean mass of $7.6 \times 10^{23}$ kg ($10^{-4}$ M_J) and an effective temperature of 668 K (10 sigma), though these values carry wide confidence intervals, particularly regarding the retrieved mass. Despite these broad limits, this study demonstrates that FSR can accurately determine an effective temperature to within a few tens of Kelvin, accurately selecting model physics, and identifying mineralogical compositions even in cold, sparse atmospheres with significant vertical mixing. These capabilities suggest the technique is transferable not just to GJ 229B but also to the emerging class of free-floating planetary candidates.

While the powerful winds of massive stars result primarily from radiative momentum transferred through spectral lines, the feebleer mass loss in solar and less massive stars stems from thermal expansion triggered by the mechanical heating of a corona. For planets orbiting these low-mass stars, the interaction of stellar radiative heating with winds can induce atmospheric heating or even ablation. The formation mechanisms diverge between stellar environments, where magnetosphemes form from trapping outgoing winds internally, whereas planetary magnetosphemes are deformed by the external stellar wind and its radiative output. These dynamics significantly alter the composition and dynamics of atmospheric outflows for both planets and stars, potentially leading to the complete stripping of a planet's atmosphere or the alteration of massive stars' final evolutionary states.

The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect involves the enhancement of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in materials positioned near an interface with a high-SOC constituent, yielding promising applications in quantum engineering. While theories for the intrinsic effect within bulk homogeneous systems exist, understanding how it manifests at interfaces between distinct materials—considering complex electronic reconstructions—is essential, particularly given that many recent applications rely on such interfaces. However, no theory has previously addressed this "extrinsic" Spin-Orbit Proximity effect. This paper presents an analytical and accessible theoretical framework capable of describing the low-energy electronic states at these interfaces. It analytically incorporates spin-resolved angular momentum reconstruction and electron accumulation/depensation phenomena, occurring due to varying potential landscapes and spin-dependent band bending. The analytical validity is tested against Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) data of an Au/Pt(111) interface, a quintessential system for illustrating the extrinsic effect.

This paper derives approximate analytic bound-state solutions for the time-independent fractional Schrödinger equation under the generalized fractional Gaussian potential, represented as $\V{V}(x) = V_0 \tanh^{2\alpha}(a x)$, where the parameter $\alpha \geq 1$. The solution method employs the Laplace transform technique, which is particularly suited for handling fractional derivatives of the Riemann-Liouville variety. Furthermore, all physical and mathematical properties of the obtained solutions are examined by presenting graphical representations of both the wave function and its probability density. Finally, through this work, the general form of the potential was utilized to study bound-state solutions of the fractional Schrödinger equation, with the illustration that this potential generalizes a wide range of forms, with $V_0$ denoting the potential depth and the parameter $\alpha a$ controlling its width. Through varying values of parameters $V_0$, $\alpha$, and $a$, both the energy and characteristics of the associated probability density exhibit significant alterations.

This study explores imposing explicit Lipschitz constraints on neural network architectures to ensure stability with respect to inputs. We introduce a method for calculating an upper bound of the Lipschitz constant across various $p$-norms for typical feedforward layers and use it to frame neural network training with bounded dynamics as a constrained optimization task soluble via projected stochastic gradients. Results reveal these models outperform those trained using standard regularizers. Furthermore, we show that the hyperparameters require only intuitive adjustment and illustrate how selecting a specific norm influences the model. Lastly, our approach yields distinct performance advantages even when only limited data is available for training.

Sequential neural network models are valuable assets across numerous Natural Language Processing applications, yet their linear architecture prompts critical inquiries: to what degree can they spontaneously master the hierarchical patterns inherent in human language, and which grammatical constructs are within their reach? Using agreement prediction in Basque as a case study—which demands implicit structural comprehension and mastery of a intricate yet orderly set of rules—we evaluate the performance of advanced attention-based sequential models. Our experimental results indicate that, despite advanced techniques, these models underperform even modest baseline approaches, falling substantially short of human accuracy levels. Consequently, these disparities offer strong empirical support for the hypothesis that basic network models possess limited capacity for hierarchical representation learning.

While modified digital games effectively foster motivation for repetitive motor rehabilitation exercises, crafting alterations that successfully meet both therapeutic and engaging objectives remains difficult. We introduce an approach utilizing a statistical model of baseline performance to determine design configurations that replicate healthy playing behaviors during adaptation to degraded inputs. Using an upper-limb rehabilitation study featuring a custom "Pac-man"-based controller to target motor recovery, we implemented this method following a collaborative design workshop with occupational therapists, who established two game-and-therapy interaction parameters. Experimental results from 12 participants confirmed that a low-latency model incorporating both user behavior patterns and in-game state data accurately predicts parameter values to emulate non-compromised play under restricted motor control. Ultimately, we outline how this methodology facilitates the systematic resolution of gamification dilemmas, effectively mediating the trade-off between physiological task necessities and enjoyable user experiences.

To address recent indications of lepton-flavour non-universality observed in $b \to c \ell \nu$ and $b \to s \ell^+ \ell^-$ decays, this investigation examines Drell-Yan dipositron pairs at CERN's LHC. Within the unpolarized scenario where $m_{B^0} < m_{LQ} < m_{t}$, robust predictions are made for the event yield at integrated luminosities of 140 fb$^{-1}$ and 3 ab$^{-1}$; notably, significant contributions from the 3 ab$^{-1}$ dataset could enable mass measurements with a precision of approximately 1 GeV. Radiation constraints inherent to positron emission tomography (PET) imaging hinder its application for studying vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, children, adults needing frequent scans, and species used in preclinical research (e.g., rats). Advances in Computed Tomography (CT)-based perfusion modeling offer a viable pathway to reduce reliance on PET. This study evaluates a hybrid imaging strategy in which [15O]H2O-PET scans are temporally aligned with high-temporal resolution, high-spatial resolution CT acquisitions. The process involves calculating perfusion parameters from jointly obtained data, utilizing the PET/CT integration to enhance the precision of CT-derived metrics through PET guidance, and leveraging the CT modalities to optimize subsequent PET reconstruction. Computed tomography scans generated specifically for perfusion analysis facilitate more precise quantification when used in conjunction with PET. Furthermore, CT measurements serve to refine low-count PET datasets by providing anatomical constraints that improve the quality of visual output.

The challenges of news curation and personalization remain unsolved. Insightful strategies by our team to create publisher-focused tools that prioritize privacy prompted a closer look at user concerns. Through survey research analyzing responses across various age demographics, this paper highlights critical findings to guide both editors and developers on refining the next wave of algorithm-driven recommendation engines, ensuring they successfully balance user experience with privacy by centering human interests.

Centering Theory (Grosz et al., 1995) analyzes how the structural components of conversation maintain local coherence through successive utterances referencing shared entities. This study explores the relationship between Centering Theory and current coreference resolution systems. We systematically assess whether neural coreference solvers align with Centering Theory rules by operationalizing the theory, constructing discourse-specific metrics, and employing a search-based framework. Results from an information-theoretic approach indicate a positive correlation between centering concepts and coreference; however, they suggest high-performing neural resolvers derive limited additional advantage from explicitly integrating these ideas. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that pretrained context-aware embeddings inherently encode much of this coherence information, which likely explains why Centering Theory yields minimal improvements for models using such representations. Lastly, we discuss known coreference drivers unmodeled by the original CT, such as world knowledge and temporal dynamics, arguing that centering-based enhancement must account for such semantic relations to be effective.

This study investigates operator growth in systems governed by Lie symmetry, applying tools from Lie algebraic methods and Krylov subspace techniques. Precise long‑baseline neutrino oscillation experiments aim to determine oscillation parameters by depending heavily on accurate neutrino-nucleus interaction models, a source of significant systematic uncertainty largely because such models struggle describing unmeasured nuclear Fermi motion. Three‑dimensionable (3‑D) projection scintillator trackers (3‑D-PST) have been established as an essential solution: they utilize the fast timing capability of scintillator detector to independently measure the x and z coordinates of incoming neutrino-nucleus collisions, thereby capturing nucleon kinetic energy alongside momentum transfer. Furthermore, the 3‑D-PST functions as a powerful tool for constructing intrinsic control datasets for experiments like DUNE and CNGS by recording simultaneous hits from high-resolution position sensors and outgoing nucleons. This letter describes initial simulations of the 3‑D-PST performed with the DAPS code, focusing on its future deployment within DUNE; simulations indicate that utilizing a front-facing 3‑D-PST could extract approximately 95% of the three‑liter (3L) liquid argon's incident nuclear momentum distribution. Using this technique introduces little bias into the extracted argon distribution and reduces related systematic errors associated with nuclear event‑by‑product simulations to roughly 1%. Additionally, the letter evaluates various 3‑D-PST material configurations and analyzes how the determined momentum distribution compares against the global EMPLA dataset.

Previous laboratory work measured how the surface energy of chondritic dust relates to moisture content by testing with pure ice, water vapor, and mixtures. Those studies found that moisture significantly boosts the force required to detach dust from pure ice, producing a strong peak at relative humidities around 10$^{-3}$ to 10$^{-2}$ that diminishes quickly as humidity rises or falls. However, this follow-up research explores surfaces coated in water vapor at interstellar levels, where dust sticks immediately to thin molecular layers separated by sub-nanometric distances. Our findings show that for grains larger than a few angstroms, sticking occurs within milliseconds across a vast range of low moisture conditions. We observed no stickiness drop-off for grains up to 0.5 $\mu$m at humidi ties as low as 10$^{-6}$, even as environmental factors like temperature and initial wetness caused the molecular films—and resulting forces—to shift. While forces generally weakened slightly with increasing distance between the dust and bulk water, they increased significantly as temperature dropped. At 20 K, forces were roughly ten times stronger than at 100 $\mu$m, positioning capillary action at these ultra-fine scales as a dominant mechanism for agglomerating chondritic particles in cool, dry molecular regions.

Consequently, frameworks based on extended movement primitives facilitate generalization in both temporal and spatial dimensions as well as in novel task conditions. Experimental validation utilizes robot arms and humanoid platforms to demonstrate the model's flexibility, spatial and temporal generalization capabilities, and robustness across various test scenarios and perturbations.

The findings indicate surface curvature alone can induce non-equilibrium positioning of chain ends within brushes, and this effect is significantly amplified by end exclusion constraints. While the focus here remains on surfaces with uniform curvature profiles, the developed framework offers a vital initial step toward addressing more intricate scenarios involving arbitrary surface roughness and chemical patterning.

A vertex subset R⊆V is called resolving if the distances from any node in G to R uniquely identify that node; the collection of all such minimum-size resolving subsets determines the graph's metric dimension. Over the past decade, numerous studies have examined various dimensions of graphs to deepen understanding of this concept. This paper continues that work by investigating the dimension of paths of trees near their centers. We demonstrate that for any ε>0, there exists δ=δ(ε)>0 ensuring the dimension of the central region in any d-dimensional graph is at least δ(ε)|V|, provided the dimension defined is not the mean k-Wtd dimension. We propose leveraging machine-learning (ML) image processing innovations to analyze all-sky maps (ASM) collected by the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope. A one-year ASM was synthetically extended from an eight-week legacy one-week image simulation through three automated techniques: "dictionary learning," "noise suppression," and "image translation." Despite noisier model estimates for an eight-week period, these algorithms produced high-fidelity ASMs indistinguishable from the legacy simulation with minimal distortion. Two automatically learned systems achieved noise reduction comparable to traditional linear de-noising algorithms without imposing the same constraints. Two robustness tests supported our approach. First, an eight-week image simulation was created using real ASM noise statistics. Second, we analyzed whether an eight-week ASM could be generated using noise suppression. Both approaches yielded ASMs consistent with linear de-noising algorithms. These findings highlight how novel ML-based image translation and noise suppression techniques enable more accurate analysis of ASM noise models compared to standard linear de-noising approaches.

Inspired by the effectiveness of serial dictatorship in social choice scenarios, we investigate its potential in solving diverse combinatorial optimization challenges. Consequently, we highlight situations—such as classroom seating, parking allocation, and resource scheduling—where this mechanism yields highly effective outcomes.

The South Atlantic rift basin, formed during the closing of the Cape Veridian shear zone in the Early Cretaceous and transitioning into the West African margin, exhibits a complex architecture that remains insufficiently understood due to sparse seismic data. By integrating well-calibrated, high-resolution seismic lines from multiple wells across the Western Nigerian portion of the site, this study applies a comprehensive seismic interpretation approach utilizing various processing strategies. Results reveal that the basin's framework consists of interconnected structural elements characterized by significant spatial and temporal variability. These features developed through progressive extension in stages, which evolved from initial WSW-ENE trending striations to final N-S oriented segments across different seismic lines. Furthermore, distinct activation ages were identified for these components; some aligns with the initial rifting phase (R1 events), while others emerged during the activation of the main onshore basin (R2 events). This phased development influenced the deposition of key stratigraphic groups, including the Pre-Salt sequence and associated seismic reflectors within Western Nigeria.

Unlabeled pre-training has emerged as a powerful strategy for enhancing various subsequent tasks when labeled data is scarce. Of the different techniques available, contrastive learning stands out for generating distinct features by establishing positive-negative pairs; however, generating meaningful pairs through an unsupervised approach is particularly difficult for image segmentation. This paper introduces an innovative unsupervised pre-training architecture that mitigates limitations inherent to contrastive learning while adhering to two foundational concepts: employing mutual information maximization via self-generated coarse segmentation as the learning pretext, and implementing learning mechanisms that preserve structural boundaries. Tests on two established medical segmentation datasets highlight the method's robustness to scarce annots, resulting in significantly boosted segmentation outcomes.

We introduce G4C (Goal-driven Guidance Generation in Grounded Communication), a new framework dedicated to investigating natural language interactions driven by specific objectives. We select Dungeons and Dragons (D&D) as our testing environment; this role-playing ecosystem brings together various player characters and a Dungeon Master, whose collective aim is to achieve player-benefitting objectives. In this setup, student characters, constrained by limited intelligence and knowledge, rely on interactions with more knowledgeable entities (such as the Dungeon Master or non-playable allies) to fulfill their goals. While the Dungeon Master constantly balances the success and enjoyment of all students, ensuring outcomes aligns with both challenge and fairness. We highlight two distinct research contributions: first, filling a gap in the role-playing game community by formally defining the Dungeon Master role and its underlying objectives within an AI research context, and second, addressing a lack of real-world data by releasing the "D&D Dataset." This large collection includes over 1,000 D&D episodes, totaling approximately 2,000 hours of expert-read audio and featuring around 30 hours of targeted human interviews. Topological insulators stand as one of the captivating topics within modern condensed matter theory. Their distinctive attributes enable the unique properties of topological materials to support unidirectional gapless electron transport as well as precise Hall conductivity measurements. While recent advancements have improved the comprehension and application of novel topological effects around Dirac/Weyl points—often utilizing artificial constructs like metamaterials, photonic crystals, and phononic systems as analogs—the study of topological properties in one-dimensional nodal lines still lags significantly. This article elucidates the fundamental theoretical framework of topological nodal lines within momentum space and evaluates both the advantages and constraints of employing phononic systems as phonological topological insulators. The discussion prioritizes two promising models: the double-extended Koster-Sathal (EKS) theory and the multiplex Berry curvature formalism. Additionally, essential features of phononic structures that foster the emergence of topological nodal lines are identified through thorough analysis. Brain tumors represent the most prevalent and fatal ailment, affecting patients across various ages. Existing studies often neglect critical issues such as varying imaging protocols, heterogeneous tumor appearances, and insufficient data availability within certain institutions. Furthermore, we developed a newly named "Domain-Adaptive Network" (DAN) framework designed specifically for generalization to other institutions using limited data. Interlace interpolation is a common approach in TV broadcasting and video recording that doubles perceived frame rates without sacrificing bandwidth, though it often introduces visible distortions like flickering and jagged edges. Accurate flow velocity superprediction across various river cross-sections is vital for effective flood management and mitigation. Although the growth of bulges remains a topic of debate, evidence supports their ongoing star formation. The results clearly demonstrate that in local systems like the M31 bulge, a higher star formation rate aligns with a lower Sersic index. This suggests that star formation occurs primarily at smaller radii where the Sersic index is low, and is most active around $z=0$, and is notably restricted to systems with radio-emitting star formation disks, such as starburst galaxies. Consequently, evolution at $z>1$ may contribute more significantly to bulge formation, as indicated by a peak in galaxy star formation rates during the epoch $1 < z < 2$. Based on this evidence regarding sustained star formation in regions of low Sersic index, the authors suggest that modern star formation processes are capable of producing the growth observed today, and are complementing mergers as key formation mechanisms.

Our solar neutron detectors, situated at high altitudes in Bolivia and Mexico, have recently started monitoring for solar neutron decay protons (NDP). These particles result from the beta-decay process of hydrogen nuclei within our solar system. While NDPs were traditionally associated with satellite-based instruments used for satellite orientation, detecting them on the ground serves as a unique signature of strong solar neutron fluxes generated by extensive air showers. Because these events are rare, we aim to distinguish ND signals from other sources, specifically cosmic ray induced NDs and atmospheric muons. Additionally, although solar ND events are uncommon, multiple NDs occurring in close temporal and spatial proximity are theoretically possible; therefore, we present Monte Carlo simulations predicting the characteristics of multi-ND events for the SND experiment.

Streaming anomaly detection involves identifying irregular data points within continuous data streams, a task that challenges both traditional and deep learning methods through issues like concept drift and the need for continuous adaptation. Leading existing algorithms often employ fixed-memory techniques such as hashing or nearest neighbors, which fail to effectively constrain rapid high-frequency values analogous to moving averages or eliminate seamless anomalies; furthermore, they cannot support end-to-end training. This study introduces an incremental approach to anomaly detection that combines random Fourier features with quantum-inspired density estimation mechanisms reminiscent of continuous exponential moving averages. Capable of handling infinite data streams while maintaining constant $O(1)$ update complexity, a comprehensive evaluation comparing the new model against twelve state-of-the-art algorithms using eighteen datasets demonstrates these results.

Laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) represents a new minimally invasive approach for ablating intracranial structures in the treatment of mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE). Segmenting the target region and surrounding anatomies from T1-weighted post-contrast MRI scans is vital for pre-treatment surgical or intra-treatment plan verification. To overcome this limitation, we created a specialized dataset consisting of 135 LITT cases. By leveraging a deep transfer learning architecture trained on our new dataset as well as the existing LITT dataset, we developed a system specifically designed to segment brain areas affected by epilepsy. Our experiments demonstrate that when using the RU-CNN in a transfer learning framework on a previously unseen case count, our method significantly outperformed other standard deep learning approaches, such as fully supervised models, MRI-guided segmentation, and manual segmentation.

GP 2 is a rule-based programming language designed to assist with verification and program analysis by utilizing transformation methods to facilitate computation. However, applications that are efficient in GP 2 face performance bottlenecks because the cost of performing graph matching is high. To overcome this challenge, GP 2 introduces rooted rules, a special category of patterns matched against restricted subgraphs defined by precomputed structures, which significantly accelerates program analysis. This paper makes the following contributions: it formally defines rooted rules within the context of GP 2, develops a semantic model ensuring consistent program executions when applying these transformations, designed an implementation strategy to realize them in GP 2, and carried out a performance evaluation demonstrating that rooted rules deliver the intended performance improvements.

Feature extraction offers a viable strategy to mitigate dimensionality challenges within high-dimensional datasets. As a prevalent self-supervised learning technique, contrastive learning has recently attracted substantial interest. In this research, we introduced a unified framework grounded in a novel interpretation of contrastive learning, applicable to both unsupervised and supervised feature extraction tasks. The framework first establishes two contrastive (CL) graphs to distinctly identify positive and negative pairs; subsequently, the projection matrix is derived by minimizing the corresponding contrastive loss function to integrate information from both similar and dissimilar examples for unifying unsupervised and supervised extraction processes. Specifically, well-known unsupervised methods—Autoencoders (AE), Deep Autoencoders (DAE), Variational Autoencoders (VAE), and their connectionist graph variants—are successfully reconstructed within this model. Additionally, leading supervised approaches, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Trees (DT), and Neural Networks (NN), are fully aligned by view as one-sided contrastive learning. Experimental results using standard datasets confirm the framework's efficacy, demonstrating its superiority over competing unsupervised and supervised methods.

Finally, you applied this framework to a Wikidata-derived biography dataset, resulting in a system that assists in generating wikiqueries and excelling at factual completion tasks involving public figures' backgrounds.

Nanometer-thick rare-earth-transition metal (RE-TM) alloys, characterized by their distinct magnetic properties and rapid dynamical behavior, hold significant promise for emerging applications in ultrafast magnetophotonic devices. However, achieving strong light-matter interactions while preserving these attributes remains a major hurdle. We synthesized FeGaN islands measuring approximately 40 nm and integrated them into vanadium oxide ($\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$) plasmonic antennas. The resulting antennas achieved resonance extinction cross-section peak at 1550 nm and demonstrated tuning of circularly polarized light absorption across the communication wavelength range through an external magnetic field, with absorption modulation reaching 35%. Furthermore, coupling the local field enhancements generated by the antennas drives ultrafast modifications in absorption driven by magnetic field shifts. Absorption dynamics exhibited picosecond-scale delays and displayed distinct colors corresponding to left and right circular polarizations under varying magnetic fields, ultimately suggesting this platform is ideal for creating all-optical, magnetic-tunable switches and modulators operating at 1550 nm.

Knowledge distillation serves as a proven strategy for expediting deep neural networks, wherein a smaller "student" model mimics the soft probability outputs of a large "teacher" network. Traditionally, this process requires access to both the input training data and the internal parameters of the white-box teacher transfer; however, constraints such as storage limits or privacy concerns in practical deployments often make these requirements unfeasible. This work introduces Decision-based Black-Box (DB3) knowledge distillation, a technique that trains a student model by extracting knowledge exclusively from a teacher where parameters are inaccessible, relying solely on inference data access and API inference. Crucially, this method captures the decisive class predictions of the teacher and employs them to generate soft labels, effectively conveying knowledge despite the opacity of the teacher's parameters. We assess this approach across various standard datasets and architectures, covering both scenarios where the teacher is accessible (gray-box) or not (black-box), thereby ensuring a robust evaluation within controlled settings as well. Results indicate that the student models trained via DB3 achieve performance closely aligned with those derived from gray-box distillation, despite the challenge of knowledge extraction from a black-box source. Additionally, experiments varying the distributional distances between teacher hard labels and true labels reveal that DB3 distillation demonstrates significant resilience to misalignment in output decisions, highlighting its reliability under noisy decision guidance.

Detecting fluctuations in the cosmic microwave background (CMB), often called anisotropies, is among the most vital techniques in cosmological research. Due to the faintness of this signal, scientists have built ever more sophisticated and sensitive instruments capable of scanning the sky across multiple frequencies with thousands of detectors sensitive to polarization. As these experiments reach higher levels of sensitivity, instrumental artifacts are often becoming the primary obstacle to fully realizing their data potential. We introduce *s4cmb* (Systematics for CMB), a Python toolkit designed to generate raw, bolometric-based time-domain data streams for current-generation CMB missions while realistically inserting instrumental systematic effects. *s4cmb* aims to assist researchers in validating analysis methods for extracting cosmological information from such data and in characterizing the precise nature of residual systematics. We detail the design and implementation of the library, demonstrating its capacity to model various sources of complexity, including electromagnetic systematics, detector and electronic behavior, and mechanical and thermal fluctuations.

Word reordering represents a language generation challenge where models must arrange unordered inputs into coherent text using ordered output, based primarily on existing research employing standard models or neural networks. Despite this history, researchers have not yet investigated the benefits of large, pre-trained language models or sought to explain why BART specifically excels at word ordering compared to other models. In this work, we performed an in-depth analysis of word ordering by first validating that BART indeed significantly outperforms its counterparts on the standard SASEval benchmark. Subsequently, we identified that BART's success stems from its ability to learn ordering relations implicitly from word contexts during pre-training. To verify this discovery, we conducted experiments on the Natural Sciences Sentence Arrangement (NS3A) task using three distinct approaches: extracting explicit ordering rules via relation extraction, generating potential orderings through prompt-based large language model generation, and training new models with these learned data. These experiments confirmed two key points: first, relationship patterns between word sequences can be explicitly defined and generated, and second, models trained on these relation-based datasets improve over those relying solely on unstructured text. To further validate the existence of such relation patterns, we demonstrated through a sliding window technique combined with a linear classifier that word ordering knowledge exists and is representable within BART’s final linguistic representations on the NS3A dataset as distinct, window-based features. Ultimately, our study confirms the central role of implicit relation learning in BART’s superior performance.

While quantum key distribution (QKD) enables unconditional secure communication over distance, real-world applications remain vulnerable to "quantum hacking" stemming from hardware limitations. In this paper, we introduce a hybrid measurement attack utilizing exclusively linear optics, single photon detection, and delay lines. This attack identifies most practical side channels—specifically, the polarization cross talk in fiber optics and beam direction in free-space systems—that provide information about an individual qubit. Consequently, an adversary can trigger the error threshold required for photon number separation (PNS) attacks without revealing other errors. We demonstrate through empirical results that this attack successfully compromises all current commercial QKD systems, including those employing time-bin, BB84, decoy-state, and Gaussian-modulated states protocols, both in laboratory settings and field deployments.

Generalized linear models were selected due to their robustness against various statistical distributions and their ability to incorporate diverse covariates for input data. Quantitative analysis using combined metrics—including Mean Absolute Percentage Error, Root Mean Square Percentage Error, and a specialized combined evaluation index—demonstrated that the proposed framework delivers superior performance in forecasting user data traffic and optimizing logical pool servers. The results also indicate that the model based on negative binomial distribution and the DR-LAP (adaptive) cross-validation approach should be adopted as the most effective model variant and cross-validation strategy, respectively, within this system.

Previous simulations by our group demonstrated that such diverse structural characteristics still facilitate the formation characteristic of observed protoplanetary systems; further research using higher-resolution smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) techniques has now validated these findings, with simulated outcomes closely matching previous results and experimental data. Our findings indicate these varying structural features significantly favor dust aggregation, with massive, low-surface-density, hierarchical systems offering ideal conditions for overcoming growth limits while minimizing gravitational fragmentation risks. This paper introduces a method for addressing regularized distributionally robust learning in a decentralized framework, specifically accounting for shifts in data distribution. By integrating a Kullback-Leibler regularization term into a robust min-max optimization, this learning task is simplified to a modified robust minimization problem solvable in great measure. Building on this newly defined formulation, we introduce a robust variant of Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Descent (DSGD), designated as the Distributionally Robust Dr-DSGD. Under mild theoretical assumptions and with the regularization parameter shrinking slowly, DR-DDSD is demonstrated to achieve a faster rate of convergence compared to its DS GD counterpart. Empirically, the results indicate that DR-DDSD not only enhances models generalization capacity but also minimizes bias towards samples with low variability. Regarding communication efficiency in message exchanges per communication round, the proposed method sacrifices only a negligible reduction compared to the standard DSGD approach.

Computing accurate estimates for pressure in the canonical hard-disk model is vital, yet existing methods suffer from excessive variance. This paper introduces an innovative, variously applicable estimator that exploits multiple canonical ensembles running at different densities to achieve superior performance. The approach relies on the fundamental and nearly universal hard-dock thermodynamic identity: $\beta P = \rho + \beta P_{\text{id}}$, where $P$ is pressure, $\beta$ the inverse of the thermal energy $k_B T$, and $\text{id}$ denotes ideal gas contributions associated with density $\rho$. While this relationship is exact, the new design mitigates the high variance typically hindering its application by leveraging these cross-density correlations. As a result, we observe a substantial reduction in variance with minimal cost, particularly for systems with low densities, without compromising the variance at the target density. The strategy proves universally applicable to hard-challenge systems with complex shapes and contact interaction potentials, yielding significantly enhanced accuracy in estimating both pressure and force.

Pyramid schemes represent investment fraud where upper-tier members of a tiered network earn commissions or free goods at the expense of lower-tier participants, with the model's collapse inevitable due to the finite size required for its operation on the foundation being built. These operations typically generate profit for established participants by incentivizing deep hierarchies that rely on continuous new enrollment. Although prevalent, accurately spotting such schemes remains difficult; our study introduces a novel detection framework by first defining their structural signature as a bipartite graph and subsequently identifying them through the examination of referral patterns. To validate our approach, we applied it to real-world data from Wikipedia edit history, successfully isolating classic pyramid structures while also flagging suspicious subgraphs for further review as potential schemes. Our methods achieve a 74% recall rate with an 84% precision level, resulting in an F1 score of 0.835. Especially when operating over extended temporal intervals, our model demonstrates high sensitivity and significantly outperforms baseline strategies.

The ongoing cataloging of globular clusters (GCs) in the Milky Way is a key initiative in astronomy. In this work, we identify 1,194 GC candidates within the Galactic bulge, expanding the known population nearly tenfold to a total of 5,324. These candidates were selected from the legless sample introduced by Anderson et al. (2014) specifically for their suitability in estimating color excess ($E(B-V)$) and total-to-selective extinction ratio ($R_V$) across bulge regions. These expansive $R_V$ and extinction maps are essential for accurate distances and stellar parameter analyses of GCs and other bulge objects, serving as critical components in projects such as the Multi-wavelength All-sky Survey Telescope Array (MAST). Based on these maps, the estimated $R_V$ range is 1.6 to 2.9, and extinction values span from 0.12 to 0.82.

Exclusive differential spectra arising from color-singlet processes at hadron colliders represent well-defined experimental observables, analyzed through parton distribution functions (PDFs). In this work, we present an examination of the Drell-Yan process and its associated virtual corrections within perturbative QCD. Specifically, we analyze how these virtual corrections influence exclusive differential spectra, utilizing two distinct definitions of the jet mass and presenting our results in terms of global PDF constraints, while also addressing the compatibility of these results with existing experimental data.

This study explores various methods for incorporating light-matter interactions within first-principles tight-binding (TB) models. While photon absorption, emission, and scattering rely on transition dipole moments—which are most accurately calculated using gauges that preserve gauge invariance—practical band structure calculations often favor the simple momentum $k$-grid of the velocity gauge due to its compatibility with fine sampling and periodic boundary conditions. However, for direct transitions between bands, gauge invariance necessitates that results from the velocity gauge be convolved with a gauge-invariant form factor. We demonstrate how these factors arise in conventional and complex periodic gauges by analyzing the relationship between the velocity and dipole gauges in the context of TB models. Although the velocity gauge can yield inaccurate gauge-dependent form factors when sampling is insufficient, the form factor remains precisely 1 in the dipole gauge, where the Berry connection vanishes. Consequently, for form factor convolution, the dipole gauge is recommended. Although convolution with a gauge-invariant form factor is computationally manageable, it introduces significant errors if applied to velocity gauge data; thus, adopting the dipole gauge offers a more accurate solution. We present form factor convolution based on the dipole gauge and apply these methods to gauge robust TB models of monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDS), showing excellent agreement with full-electron density functional theory for both monoelectronic and gauge-sensitive many-electronic scenarios.

Certain architectures in quantum error correcting codes allow for the direct implementation of multi-qubit gates that encode logical operations, potentially bypassing the need for transversal circuit synthesis and significantly cutting down circuit depth at the physical level. We present a novel algorithm designed to construct high-weight gates acting directly on multiple encoded qubits within these specific error corrected codes. This approach prioritizes minimizing the use of gates that interact with qubits outside the code block (boundary gates) and prefers gates with greater interaction weights (higher weight is better to avoid boundaries). Furthermore, our strategy targets scenarios where the available gate set is restricted by hardware constraints, and it operates exclusively using gates permitted by those limitations to execute an arbitrary desired operation. Confining error coding logic within a localized region enhances fault tolerance by diminishing the complexity and limitations imposed by interconnects between qubits. Lastly, we establish that utilizing heavier gates is computationally efficient, offering a speed advantage over equivalent circuits composed of lower-weight gates.

Accurate tissue segmentation serves as a crucial prerequisite for enhancing our comprehension of tissue architecture and, consequently, improving cancer diagnostics and therapy monitoring. An exemplary scenario involves distinguishing between healthy and malignant prostate regions by segmenting various prototypical units—such as glands, lumens, and whole tumors—as well as broader anatomical zones like peripheral and transition tumor zones of the prostate. However, effectively segmenting these heterogeneous tissue components necessitates capturing multiple spatial scales. This study introduces a novel full-scale convolutional neural architecture (FS-CNN) specifically designed to integrate semantic information across different scales to enhance prostate cancer diagnosis. To populate this model with comprehensive contextual data, we developed a unique labeling strategy for histological structures that enables the FS-CNN. Validated on a substantial dataset of 900 digitized prostatectomy whole-slide images, the model was tested against a high-resolution standard. The results indicate that the FS-CNN not only matches but in certain instances surpasses the expertise of pathologists in terms of consistency and accuracy. Subjective evaluation by a panel also confirmed these objective metrics, establishing the FS-CNN as a robust framework to assist in accurate cancer diagnosis.

Multivariate point processes are extensively used to analyze events characterized by type, such as neural firing patterns, financial transactions, and digital communications. Among these, the Hawkes process stands as a prominent model, capturing dependencies through the process history and facilitating cause-and-effect relationships. However, accounting for these dynamic mechanisms often requires significant computational resources and complex inference techniques. This paper introduces OPTIMAL-HAWKES, an efficient framework designed to estimate both fixed and time-dependent causal kernels and their parameters directly from event-type data. By formulating the estimation task as an optimization problem and applying gradient-based methods, our approach handles high-dimensional inputs and successfully estimates self-excitatory and inhibitive dependencies across various process pairs. Experimental results indicate that in terms of likelihood scores, predicted event rates, and the practical application in reconstructing causal graphs, our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms. Additionally, our technique offers the distinct advantages of enhanced scalability and explicit interpretability.

Smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) is celebrated for maintaining highly accurate conservation properties; when executed correctly, it precisely conserves total mass, energy, and both linear and angular momenta up to floating-point limits. This exactness is crucial for computational astrophysical tasks like studying binary mergers or x-ray flares. However, standard SPH fails to conserve individual components of linear and angular momentum during close binary encounters, a deficiency that can generate spurious forces, or "noise," between stars. Resolving this has long been a high priority. Our prior work achieved this for binary systems confined to a single plane by employing an implementation of three-dimensional (3D) SPH restricted to two dimensions (2D). In this study, we extend that 2D+2 model to the full three dimensions (3D), enabling the simulation of general, three-dimensional binary scenarios. Our findings indicate that while this generalized 3D scheme drastically reduces dynamical noise compared to conventional two-dimensional (2D) approaches—improving accuracy by orders of magnitude—it still conserves only the planar components of linear and angular momentum. Consequently, although noise is greatly diminished within single planes, it remains present out of plane. This leads us to conclude that SPH cannot simultaneously ensure precise conservation up to numerical precision for the three dimensions of linear and angular momentum components. Nevertheless, this specialized 2D formula applied to collinear mergers represents a valuable research tool.

Although Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have reached state-of-the-art levels in medical image segmentation, they depend heavily on extensive manual annotations for training. Semi-Supervised Learning (SSL) approaches offer a path to reducing annotation needs, yet they struggle to accommodate large annotated datasets commonly found in medical fields like Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD). Addressing this limitation, we offer a novel Fully Supervised Learning (LSI) framework based on Bayesian Co-Adaptation that assumes low annotational noise and leverages prior knowledge about anatomical structures. By integrating this assumption into a fully supervised Bayesian approach, we derive a closed-form solution for updating model parameters. The proposed method is computationally efficient, requiring no unlabeled data training, and features very high performance with virtually zero annotation need. Our method has been tested on two publicly available datasets: the Brain Tumor Segation (MSD) dataset and the Kidney Segmentation (KIWA) dataset, showing significantly higher Dice Similarity Coefficients compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, especially when utilizing anatomical priors. We also provide a comparative analysis across different datasets, confirming the method's robustness when adapting models between source and target tasks without retraining using prior structural knowledge.
